Surah al-Infitar

Allah, Exalted and Majestic, says: ﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder, and when the stars are scattered, and when the seas are burst forth, and when the graves are overturned, [then] a soul will know what it has put forth and what it has left behind.﴾ [al-Infitar 1-5]. These are four things which, when they occur, will make every soul know what it sent forward in the beginning of its life and what it left behind.

As for His saying ﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder﴾, it means: split open, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿When the sky splits open, and it listens to its Lord and it is obligated to do so﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 1-2].

﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾ means: the stars, small and large, will be scattered, dispersed and fall, because the world will have come to an end.

﴿And when the seas are burst forth﴾ means: some of them will be made to burst into others, and they will fill the earth.

﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾ means: what is in them of the dead will be brought out, until they stand before Allah, Exalted and Majestic.

When these four matters occur, ﴿a soul will know what it has put forth and what it has left behind.﴾ Here ﴿soul﴾ (nafs) is indefinite, but it carries a general meaning, since the meaning is: every soul will know what it has put forth and what it has left behind. This will be through the record that is presented to it. Every person has had his bird of fate (ta'ir) fastened to his neck by Allah, and on the Day of Resurrection He will bring forth for him a book which he will meet wide open: ﴿Read your record. Sufficient is your soul against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra 14].

On that Day the criminals will say: ﴿What kind of record is this, that leaves out nothing small or great but has counted it?﴾ [al-Kahf 49]. So man will know what he sent forward and what he left behind, whereas in this world he had forgotten. We now have forgotten what we did long ago, but on the Day of Resurrection our deeds will be presented to us, and every soul will know what it sent forward and what it left behind.

The purpose of this warning is to caution the servant against doing anything that opposes Allah and His Messenger, because he will come to know of it and will be held accountable for it.

﴿O humankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ [Al-Infitar 6]. ﴿O humankind﴾: the word al-insan (الإنسان, "the human being") here is said by some to mean the disbeliever, and by others to mean the human being as such, since the human being as such is ﴿truly wrongdoing, ignorant﴾, ﴿truly wrongdoing, ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim 34].

So Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿O humankind﴾, addressing the human being as such, setting aside his religion. ﴿What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ That is, what has deceived you about Allah, that you deny Him in the resurrection and disobey Him in His commands and prohibitions? Indeed, there are those who deny Allah, mighty and majestic altogether, so what has deceived you?!

Some scholars said: the words of the Exalted, ﴿What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ point to the answer, which is that what deceived the human being is the generosity of Allah, mighty and majestic, His granting of respite and His forbearance. But it is not permissible for a person to be deceived by this, for Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, and when He seizes him, He does not let him go.

So: what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? The answer: His generosity and His forbearance. This is what has deceived the human being, so he keeps persisting in disobedience, persisting in denial, persisting in opposition.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 82, verse 7:

﴿Who created you, then proportioned you, and then balanced you﴾ [al-Infitar: 7]. He created you from nothing, and brought you into existence from nothing. ﴿Sawwaka﴾ (proportioned you) means He made you of balanced form: no hand is longer than the other hand, no leg is longer than the other leg, and no finger is longer than another finger, in keeping with the two hands and the two legs. So you find that the long one in one hand is long in the other hand too, and the short one is short, and so on. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made the human being balanced in every respect of his creation.

﴿Fa'adalaka﴾ (then balanced you). In one of the seven recitations it is ﴿fa'addalaka﴾ (with the doubled dal). It means: He made you of upright stature and balanced form, unlike the beasts, which were not made balanced but walk on their hands and feet. As for the human being, Allah has singled him out with this distinction.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 82, verse 8:

﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you.﴾ [Al-Infitar: 8] Meaning: Allah assembled you in whatever form He willed. Among people there is the beautiful, and among them the ugly, and among them the average, and among them the white, and among them the red, and among them the black, and among them what lies between these. Whatever form Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assembles you in is according to His will. Yet He, Mighty and Majestic, willed for the human being that his form be the best of forms.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, but you deny the Recompense (ad-Din).﴾ [Al-Infitar 9] ﴿Nay﴾ is a particle of restraint, and "bal" (but/rather) is for turning away from the previous statement. It means: despite this creation, this provision, and this preparation, you deny the Din (ad-Din), that is, the Recompense (al-jaza'), and you say: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 37] So you deny the Din, that is, the Recompense. Perhaps we may also say: you also deny the Din itself, so you do not acknowledge the religion that the messengers brought. The verse includes both of these meanings, because the rule in the science of tafsir and the science of explaining hadith is that when a text can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is taken to mean both of them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 82, verses 10–12:

﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know whatever you do.﴾ [al-Infitar: 10-12], an emphasis with two emphasizers (inna) and the lam (of emphasis). ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians﴾: every person has a guardian who preserves him, and who records everything he does. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Not an utterance does he utter except that with him is an observer, ready [to record]﴾ [Qaf: 18].

So over every person are guardians (hafazah) who write down everything he says and everything he does. These guardians are noble (kiram), not base; they possess such nobility that it precludes them from wronging anyone by recording against him what he did not do, or by discarding what he did do, since they are described as noble.

﴿They know what you do﴾: either by witnessing it if it is an action, or by hearing it if it is a statement. Moreover, Allah makes them aware of the deeds of the heart so that they record them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; and whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a complete good deed is recorded for him" [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (6491), and Muslim (131/207), from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)]; because he left it for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The former is rewarded merely for the intention of a good deed.

Verse 13: "Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss." This is an explanation of the final outcome and the reward.

"Indeed, the righteous" (al-abrar) is the plural of barr, those who do much good and keep far away from evil. "Will be in bliss" (lafi na'im) means: bliss of the heart and bliss of the body. That is why we find no one with a better heart or more at ease in mind than the righteous people of piety (ahl al-birr). Some of the early pious predecessors (salaf) said: "If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us over it with swords." This bliss exists both in this world and in the Hereafter. In the Hereafter it is Paradise (al-Jannah). In this world it is the bliss of the heart, its tranquility, and its contentment with Allah's decree and His destiny, for this is truly bliss. Bliss in this world is not that one is pampered in body; bliss is the bliss of the heart.

﴿Indeed, the wicked will surely be in Hellfire﴾ [al-Infitar: 14]. The wicked (al-Fujjar) are the disbelievers, the opposite of the righteous (al-Abrar). ﴿Will surely be in Hellfire﴾, meaning: in a blazing fire, may Allah protect us.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 82, verse 15:

﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Infitar: 15]. Meaning: they will be burned by it. ﴿On the Day of Recompense﴾, i.e., the Day of Judgment, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 82, verse 16:

﴿And they will not be absent from it.﴾ [Al-Infitar: 16] Meaning: they will never be absent from it so as to be taken out of it, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And they will not be removed from it.﴾ [Al-Hijr: 48], because they will be abiding in it forever, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 82, verses 17–18:

﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is? (17) Then what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ [Al-Infitar: 17, 18] This interrogative form (istifham, a rhetorical question) is for magnification and exaltation. It means: "What has informed you about the Day of Recompense?" Its meaning is: know this Day and esteem it its proper esteem. ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ ﴿ ﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 82, verse 19:

﴿On that Day no soul will have power to do anything for another soul, and the Command on that Day will be entirely with Allah﴾ [al-Infitar: 19]. On the Day of Resurrection, no one has power to bring benefit to anyone or to ward off harm from anyone, except by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; this is because of His saying: ﴿and the Command on that Day will be entirely with Allah﴾. In this world there are people who give orders: rulers (umara'), ministers (wuzara'), presidents (ru'asa'), fathers and mothers. But in the Hereafter there is none of this; the command belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and no soul will have power over another soul except by Allah's permission.

For this reason, on that Day people will suffer distress and anguish beyond what they can bear. Then they will seek intercession (shafa'ah) from Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, until they reach our Prophet (ﷺ), and he will intercede by Allah's permission, and Allah will relieve all creation from the place of standing.

﴿and the Command on that Day will be entirely with Allah﴾. If someone says: Is not the command Allah's on that Day and on other days as well?

We say: Yes, the command belongs to Allah the Exalted on the Day of Judgment and before it; but the manifestation of His command on that Day is far greater than its manifestation in this world. In this world a person opposes the commands of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and obeys the orders of his master, so the command is not Allah's in his case. But in the Hereafter there is no command except the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whose is the Kingdom today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. Sovereignty belongs to Allah both in this world and in the Hereafter, but on that Day the dominion (malakut) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His command become manifest, and it becomes clear that there is no one who commands on that Day except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
